video_title: Coach Daigneault on OKC's West Coast Road Trip | Postgame Media | November 15, 2026

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on Lu Dort's energy and growth
quotes.excerpt: It's a good experience for him understanding you got to get yourself back to the bottom of the mountain
quotes.quote: I thought a guy like Lu Dort tonight, his first stretch, I didn't think his energy was where it normally is and then he got into the game and played better as he went. So it's a good experience for him understanding you got to get yourself back to the bottom of the mountain every night and you got to start climbing. So he had a great game, but it took him a minute to get there.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault on Lu Dort after tonight's win: It is a good experience for him understanding you have to get yourself back to the bottom of the mountain every night and you have to start climbing.

structured.context: Mark Daigneault discusses Lu Dort's performance and energy levels during the postgame media availability.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on AJ Mitchell's impact and return
quotes.excerpt: He's obviously a high-impact player that can give us a lot of minutes
quotes.quote: He's obviously a high-impact player that can give us a lot of minutes and he helps us on both ends of the floor. So you add that back in, it's pretty significant for us. So it's good to have him back out there and obviously we can keep building from here, but it definitely helps us.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault on the return of AJ Mitchell: He is a high impact player that can give us a lot of minutes and he helps us on both ends of the floor. It is pretty significant for us.

structured.context: Mark Daigneault comments on the impact of AJ Mitchell returning to the lineup after an absence.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on Nick Smith Jr.'s professionalism and integration
quotes.excerpt: He wants to be a part of the team, he wants to win, he wants to compete
quotes.quote: I just think he wants to be a part of the team, he wants to win, he wants to compete. So it doesn't surprise me that he went out there and played the way he did. I thought his defense in the second half specifically, and he was part of that group to start the fourth, was really good. Probably the best it's been in the couple games he's played with us. More physical on the ball, good on the pursuits, and started to get his feet underneath him on that end of the floor. So that was encouraging, he gave us good minutes. One of the things Sam has done a great job of is recognizing that everyone we add to the team has to be able to hop on that train and he's got those qualities. He's professional, he's hardworking, he's about the team, he wants to get better, he wants to do it inside of the team and that allows you to integrate very easily here, as we've seen with guys like McCain and our rookie players.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault on integrating Nick Smith Jr: He wants to win and he wants to compete. He is professional and hardworking and that allows you to integrate very easily here.

structured.context: Mark Daigneault praises Nick Smith Jr.'s professionalism and integration into the team culture.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on managing rotation and player trust
quotes.excerpt: We need to trust our whole roster and we need to develop our whole roster
quotes.quote: We're trying to be an 82-game team and we need to trust our whole roster and we need to develop our whole roster. So we have to put pressure on the whole team to perform in all 48 minutes. We can't always go back to not only Shai, but starters or high-minute guys. We'll push them at certain times, he played 30-something minutes the other night, 38 I think against the Clippers, and then on nights like tonight, we let those other guys go and close the thing.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault on managing the Thunder rotation: We are trying to be an 82 game team and we need to trust our whole roster. We cannot always go back to not only Shai but starters or high minute guys.

structured.context: Mark Daigneault explains the team's philosophy on managing player minutes and rotation depth.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on team response to injuries
quotes.excerpt: If you have to change your principles based on the circumstances then you have the wrong principles
quotes.quote: Initially when it first happened, if I'm being completely honest, the team had an appropriate human response. It's a couple guys that have worked incredibly hard that are going to be knocked out for a long period of time, which has an impact not only on our team but on them. There was a level of empathy and it was certainly an unpredictable circumstance. So I'd be lying if I said we just flipped the switch and kept moving. There was an appropriate period of time that we allowed that processing to happen. But in terms of what we lean on, we lean on the same things. Your circumstances are always changing but our principles aren't. I've said this many times, but if you have to change your principles based on the circumstances then you have the wrong principles. We really don't change much in any circumstance, we lean on the things that we're about and trust those things and these guys do a great job of bringing that to life.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault on the team's reaction to recent injuries: The team had an appropriate human response. I would be lying if I said we just flipped the switch and kept moving. There was an appropriate period of time we allowed that to happen.

structured.context: Mark Daigneault reflects on how the team processed the news of recent long-term injuries to teammates.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's workload and development
quotes.excerpt: Getting AJ back was huge because that relieves some of the ball-handling duties
quotes.quote: We're trying to compete and win every game as we always do. How we do that is dependent on who's available obviously, the calculus changes with the guys that we have out right now. But the same things are intact. We don't want to overwork anybody and he's worked really hard on expanding his game and we try to bring that to life. Getting AJ back was huge because that relieves some of the ball-handling duties and allows us to move him around the floor a little bit more, which we'll continue to do. But he's done a great job of, like I said, the circumstances you can't control, but he's been the exact same as he always is. He's been a great leader, he's been a great performer, even in this, we just lost a couple tough games in a row and just the tone he set tonight, he doesn't panic, he just goes out there and plays.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault on Shai Gilgeous Alexander: Getting AJ back was huge because that relieves some of the ball handling duties and allows us to move him around the floor a little bit more.

structured.context: Mark Daigneault discusses Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's leadership and how AJ Mitchell's return affects the team's ball-handling rotation.
